title: Telemetry watermarking and client-visible freshness indicators for usage charts
creator: Ethan Liu
description:
Problem summary:
Customers and internal dashboards are showing spikes and troughs in per-model cost/usage charts that do not align with raw event counts. These artifacts are primarily visible when there is a delayed ingestion/backfill window (e.g., 30m-12h after generation) and when rate-limit credits are applied retroactively. The console currently provides no explicit indication of data freshness or provenance for affected time buckets, making it hard for engineers and customers to reason about whether a visible change is a real behavior shift or an ingestion reconciliation.

Observed user impact:
- Product teams see sudden model cost regressions and open P1s.
- Support escalations from customers who believe billing is incorrect.
- Dashboard-driven alerts (anomaly detectors) firing on backfill-induced volatility.

Goals for this ticket:
1) Add an ingest watermark and display a freshness/provenance indicator on Console charts (per-model breakdowns and top-models) so users can quickly tell whether recent bars are provisional.
2) Implement deterministic attribution for retroactive rate-limit credit adjustments so the Console shows a transparent reconciliation delta (not silently mutate historical bars).
3) Provide an internal audit trace linking UI buckets to the ingest window and reconciliation job run IDs so SREs and billing support can triage rapidly.
proposed_solution:
High-level approach:
1) Ingest watermarking: propagate an ingest_watermark timestamp through the event pipeline and attach provenance tags to aggregated bucket rows: source='stream'|'backfill', ingestion_time, ingestion_run_id. Surface a small freshness badge on any chart bucket where ingestion_time is within the last 48h and differs from event_time by > 5 minutes.
2) Credit reconciliation path: change the ledger mutator to write reconciliation events (RCV- entries) into the same event stream with an explicit reconciliation_reason and reconciliation_run_id. Aggregator will emit a separate reconciliation_delta series for affected buckets instead of rewriting base counts. The console UI will stack 'base' + 'reconciliation_delta' visually and allow toggling reconciliation visibility.
3) UI & explainability: add a hover tooltip showing provenance (original event timestamp, ingestion_time, run id, contributor shard) and a legend explaining provisional vs committed data.
4) Backfill dry-run: a new non-destructive dry-run mode for the reconciliation job to preview deltas for the last 7 days and produce an explainability report for customer support prior to applying final reconciliations.

Engineering trade-offs:
- Storing provenance increases row width in the aggregated store; to limit cost we will compress provenance into short ids and maintain a separate run metadata table for human-readable info.
- Emitting reconciliation as delta series increases chart complexity; however it avoids silent mutation and preserves an audit trail.

Implementation phases (this ticket covers phase 1+2 prototype):
- Phase A (this ticket): add ingest_watermark propagation, write reconciliation events as deltas, basic Console badge + tooltip.
- Phase B: durable run metadata UI, dry-run job, and analytics-driven heuristic to auto-suppress low-quality backfills in customer-facing charts.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows a freshness badge on time series buckets where ingestion_time - event_time > 5 minutes for recent 48h
Reconciliation events appear as a separate stacked series in per-model breakdown charts and can be toggled off/on
Audit links for at least 95% of reconciled buckets surface run_id and link to the reconciliation job log in internal tools
Dry-run produces a reconciliation delta preview that matches the applied reconciliation within rounding error for test datasets
No regression on existing SLOs for chart load time (>95th pctile unchanged) for typical tenant dashboards
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy ingest_watermark propagation to staging and enable on a small traffic tenant group (canary).
2) Ship aggregator change in read-only mode that exposes reconciliation_delta in a hidden series; validate dry-run outputs against current backfill job outputs.
3) Release UI badge and toggle in closed beta to internal teams and selected customers.
4) After 72h of canary, flip reconciliation delta to be visible to all; continue monitoring support tickets and chart latency.
5) Run a 2-week watch with postmortem if any unexpected billing deltas occur.
comments: 2026-03-10 Ethan Liu: Initial triage — spike shows provenance mismatches between shard ingest times. Repro script attached to the confluence doc.
2026-03-11 Maya Patel: Scoped to prototype for phase A. Agreed to avoid immediate schema change by compressing provenance into run IDs and separate metadata table.

2026-03-12 SRE (Jonas Kim): Concerned about extra writes during peak. Proposed rate-limit for reconciliation dry-run and batching of run metadata writes — we will implement a small buffer with fsync boundaries.
2026-03-12 PM (Lina Gomez): Please ensure support can toggle reconciliation series per-tenant from the Console; Lina approved the UX microcopy for badge and tooltip.

2026-03-13 Maya Patel: Prototype aggregator change merged to staging branch github://redwood/aggregator/pull/5123. Running integration tests against replay dataset now. Observed an average chart load latency increase of 4% in staging (within acceptable range).
